name: Saint Thomas Aquinas
history: A Dominican friar from southern Italy whose Summa Theologiae is the greatest synthesis of Catholic theology. He showed that faith and reason come from the same God and cannot finally contradict each other. He wrote the hymns of Corpus Christi, among them the Pange Lingua and Tantum Ergo. He is called the Angelic Doctor and is patron of Catholic schools and universities.
life: Thomas was born at Roccasecca, near Aquino, into a noble family who sent him at five to the abbey of Monte Cassino, hoping he would one day be its abbot. At Naples he met the new Order of Preachers and joined it. His family seized him on the road and kept him at home for a year, but he would not be moved. He studied under Saint Albert the Great at Cologne, where his silence earned him the name of the dumb ox; Albert replied that this ox would one day bellow so loud that the whole world would hear. He taught at Paris, Rome and Naples and wrote with astonishing speed. In December 1273, after an experience at Mass, he stopped writing, leaving the Summa unfinished. Summoned to the Council of Lyon, he fell ill on the way and died at the Cistercian abbey of Fossanova on 7 March 1274. Today’s date marks the translation of his relics to Toulouse.
prayerTo: Saint Thomas, you used every gift of mind in the service of truth and knelt in wonder before the Eucharist. Pray for students, teachers and all who seek the truth, that they may find it in Christ. Pray for me, that I may love God with all my mind, think clearly and stay humble before the mystery. Amen.
prayer: Godhead here in hiding, whom I do adore, masked by these bare shadows, shape and nothing more, see, Lord, at thy service low lies here a heart lost, all lost in wonder at the God thou art.
prayerSource: Saint Thomas Aquinas, Adoro te devote, translated by Gerard Manley Hopkins
penance: Spend time before the Blessed Sacrament today, or pray the Tantum Ergo slowly, and offer your work or study for the glory of God.
meditation: At the end he said that all he had written seemed like straw compared with what he had seen. Of all you are busy with, what will matter in the end?
